section_summary.extract_value: This section reports descriptive statistics comparing the current sample of Black women to previously published college samples: the current sample had higher average Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) scores than the Avalos et al. (2005) development sample (primarily White college students) and lower average EDE-Q-R and EDE-Q-EC scores than Luce et al. (2008); some EDE-Q subscales did not differ significantly. The note clarifies that BAS refers to the Body Appreciation Scale.
section_summary.evidence_source: 'The current sample of Black women reported higher average BAS scores than the development sample (comprising primarily White college students; Avalos et al., 2005), t(545) = 6.75, p < .001.'; 'The current sample also endorsed lower average scores on the EDE-Q-R, t(949) = 4.53, p < .001, and the EDE-Q-EC, t(949) = 3.15, p = .002, than the sample of undergraduate women examined by Luce, Crowther, and Pole (2008). Average scores on the EDE-Q-SC, t(947) = 2.09, p = .037, and the EDE-Q-WC, t(947) = .80, p = .422, did not differ significantly between the two samples.'; 'Note. BAS = Body Appreciation Scale.'
